title: Small town life; advantages and disadvantages
description: Audrey Winter contrasts rural living in Kellogg with broader world awareness. She discusses isolation but also safety and community vigilance regarding children.

title: Childhood in Kellogg; married life adjustment
description: Winter describes her sheltered upbringing after her father's death and the drastic transition to her husband's rural lifestyle. She details the lack of modern conveniences in early homes.

title: Homemaking without modern conveniences
description: She recounts learning to heat water, wash clothes, and cook without plumbing or electricity. These hardships taught her self-sufficiency and gave her new appreciation for her parents' sacrifices.

title: Railroad work and economic hardships
description: Discussion of her husband's railroad employment, frequent layoffs, and the necessity of hunting to ensure food security during difficult times.

title: Childhood memories and family gatherings
description: Winter recalls holidays and birthdays with her siblings, including humorous anecdotes about embarrassing childhood moments involving her sister and uncle.

title: Courtship and meeting husband
description: She describes delivering a message to her future husband's sister and the circumstances of their meeting. She explains the beginning of their relationship.

title: Marriage conflicts and family opposition
description: Winter details the family conflict surrounding her decision to marry at age 18. She describes her mother's initial disapproval and her sister's belief that she should remain home to care for their mother.

title: Early marriage expectations; pregnancy
description: Discussion of unrealistic expectations about marriage and the surprise of her first pregnancy six weeks after the wedding. She notes her lack of knowledge about contraception.

title: First childbirth; early parenthood
description: She recounts the difficult 17-hour labor for her first child, Nancy. She reflects on the challenges of adjusting to parenthood and the advice she received from family members.

title: Raising children; hopes for daughter
description: Winter discusses her parenting philosophy and her desire for her daughter to experience life away from Kellogg. She considers the importance of children establishing independence from their parents.

title: Family activities; Christian faith
description: She explains the family's recreational activities and their Christian faith. She mentions reading materials and the influence of her beliefs on child-rearing.

title: Widowhood and widowhood concerns
description: Winter contemplates the possibility of her husband's death or serious illness. She considers how she would manage as a single parent and the importance of continued faith.

title: Future plans; daughter's activities
description: Audrey Winter considers staying at her current high-paying job while contemplating further education. She expresses concern that her daughter Nancy will miss opportunities in their remote location, and would commute to Saint Mary's to ensure she can participate in school activities.

title: Parenting advice; marital roles
description: Winter offers hypothetical advice to her daughter about rushing into marriage and the importance of sex education. She discusses her household financial arrangement, where her husband has final authority but they share resources, and describes how he has learned to share domestic duties since she began working.

title: Church involvement; rural isolation
description: Winter explains her husband's limited participation in church activities compared to her own Christian practice. She describes missing city amenities like shopping, the challenges of winter travel on rural roads, and the extra effort required to participate in activities from their remote location.

title: Health care; mill accidents
description: Winter criticizes the local hospital's staff and limited services, describing her difficult childbirth experience and preference for hospitals in larger cities. She recounts mill accidents involving her husband and others, and mentions community first aid training.

title: Community support
description: Winter recounts caring for a dying neighbor and receiving training to give medical shots. She emphasizes the strong community support system where neighbors help each other during illnesses, financial problems, and emergencies.

title: Home repairs; mail service
description: Winter describes how residents handle their own repairs due to the expense and unreliability of outside help, including their experience with a broken furnace. She explains the local mail service, which includes medication delivery from Saint Mary's but sometimes misdirects mail to towns with similar names.

title: Flood evacuation and survival; community recovery
description: Audrey Winter recounts being flooded out of her home and evacuating to Saint Marys during a severe winter flood, losing electricity and relying on generators to save food. She describes how the community pulled together during the disaster, with churches collecting offerings and residents helping rebuild, though some homes in Riverdale were completely destroyed by mud and water.

title: Mill work and picket grading
description: Winter explains her job at the lumber mill where she wears a hard hat and grades wooden pickets by quality and size, distinguishing between straight and fancy pointed styles for sale to Sears. She describes learning the judgment skills required for the fast-paced work.

title: Piece work and women employees
description: The interview continues with discussion of payment by the piece rather than hourly, with Winter explaining that a good day yields two hundred pieces. She notes that up to twenty women have worked at the mill at one time, sometimes splitting shifts.

title: Physical labor and local economy
description: Winter describes the physically demanding nature of lifting fifty-pound bundles and constant bending required by the job. She notes that the mill is the main employer for Calder, alongside logging, PFI, and the Milwaukee railroad where her husband worked on the section crew.
